summary: Gate skill adoption on a resource-aware paired evaluation: before enabling a skill, run the same task set with-skill vs without-skill in isolated runs and compare pass-rate improvement against token, time (and where measurable, tool-call/turn) overhead; adopt only when the quality gain justifies the resource delta under a pre-declared budget. This is directly supported by official tooling — Anthropic's skill-creator provides isolated per-case eval runs recording token count and duration, and a Benchmark mode aggregating pass rate, time, and tokens for with-skill versus without-skill into benchmark.json 'so you can compare the pass-rate improvement against the token and time overhead' — and by both papers: SWE-Skills-Bench demonstrates that only paired measurement distinguishes the minority of net-positive skills (7/49) from no-gain/high-overhead ones, and arXiv 2608.11888 recommends cost-aware skill selection that predicts extra exploration/verification/implementation work before choosing a skill. Tessl's 880-eval field benchmark shows the practice is operationally feasible at scale.

evidence.summary: skill-creator eval features: isolated subagent runs recording token count and duration; Benchmark aggregates pass rate, time, and tokens for with-skill vs without-skill into benchmark.json for gain-vs-overhead comparison.
'Build evaluations first': establish a no-skill baseline, write minimal instructions, require at least three evaluations; evals are 'your source of truth for measuring Skill effectiveness'.
Paired with/without benchmark shows 39/49 skills give no pass-rate gain while token overhead reaches +451%; supports measurement-first, domain-fit-specific adoption decisions.
Recommends cost-aware skill packaging and selection: estimate marginal context cost and predict extra exploration, implementation, verification work before selecting a skill.
880-eval field benchmark measuring cost, input tokens, and turns per skill/model configuration demonstrates operational feasibility of resource-aware skill evaluation.

requires: representative task set for the skill's domain
harness able to run isolated with/without comparisons and record tokens and duration (e.g. Anthropic skill-creator eval/benchmark)
a pre-declared adoption budget for acceptable resource overhead per unit of quality gain
not_for: skills whose value is non-quantifiable compliance/safety behavior where resource cost is accepted by policy
environments unable to run repeated evals (cost of evaluation itself must stay proportionate)

revalidate_when: a standard adoption threshold trading quality vs resource overhead is published
major model generation change alters skill cost/benefit profiles
risks: Eval task sets may not represent production task mix; a skill can pass the gate yet regress on unmeasured task types
Tool-call counts are not an explicitly documented skill-creator benchmark metric; may require additional harness telemetry
Model variance requires repeated runs for stable deltas, adding eval cost

matched_on: documented eval features: isolated runs recording token count and duration
with-skill vs without-skill benchmark aggregating pass rate, time, and tokens

evidence: Documented in official Claude Code docs as the skill creation/eval tooling (Anthropic, provider-official)
Used as eval engine by the shared skill-optimization plugin
